claims.text: Subtle changes in Al content alter the extent of local short-range ordering in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Local short-range ordering governs phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Short-range ordering stabilizes an ordered BCC or B2 phase.
The ordered BCC or B2 phase is responsible for favorable high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
A homogenized alloy containing approximately 15 at.% Al has incipient short-range order and a mixed microstructure.
Increasing Al from approximately 15 at.% to approximately 20 at.% under an identical heat treatment will enable greater short-range-order development.
Maintaining Al between approximately 13 and 20 at.% avoids extensive precipitation of uncontrolled secondary phases.
Pair distribution function analysis or atom probe tomography can characterize the degree and nature of local short-range order and associated elemental partitioning.
Increasing Al promotes specific interatomic interactions that enhance short-range-order formation.
Al-enhanced local ordering selectively stabilizes an ordered BCC or B2 phase.
The stabilized ordered phase underpins overall phase stability and the balance of mechanical and environmental properties.
Relative to the approximately 15 at.% Al baseline, the higher-Al alloy will contain a larger fraction of the ordered phase.
The higher-Al alloy will have greater high-temperature strength because of stabilization of the ordered phase.
The higher-Al alloy will have greater radiation resistance because of stabilization of the ordered phase.
Increasing Al may cause a slight reduction in cryogenic toughness.
The proposed mechanism is limited to approximately 13–20 at.% Al and thermal conditions that permit short-range-order development.
Outside the stated composition and processing boundaries, other phase-transformation mechanisms may dominate.
Failure of increased Al to increase short-range order or stabilize the ordered phase, together with failure of the tested properties to shift as predicted, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The ordered BCC/B2 phase is described as responsible for favorable cryogenic toughness, yet increasing its fraction is predicted to reduce cryogenic toughness. This inverse relationship is not reconciled mechanistically.

The alloys are said to be identical except for Al, while the design also says to increase Al and keep all other elements constant. In atomic-percent compositions, increasing Al necessarily changes the normalized percentages of the other elements unless a specific substitution or fixed-ratio scheme is defined.
